verdict.rationale: AWS documents the building blocks. Assumed IAM roles issue temporary session credentials with no long-term keys (aws-docs-12, aws-docs-46), and policies, including permissions boundaries, scope and cap what an identity can do (aws-docs-11, aws-docs-28). AgentCore says it handles authentication and access control for agents calling tools and APIs (aws-docs-24, aws-docs-35). However, the evidence never ties these into an explicit agent-credential pattern, and the AgentCore claims are marketing-level. Missing for 10: a documented agent-specific pattern for scoped temporary credentials, explicit detail on how escalation is prevented (session policies or how boundaries block self-escalation), and independent or hands-on corroboration.
